_doc: The validation ledger (Christian, 12 Nov 2026: 'Independent validation is very important. keep track of these and quantify them for the final report'). One entry per claim of the camera and rig models with the evidence that does not come from the joints. level: A internal (residuals, leave-one-out), B new data with the same method, C a different measurement. status: confirmed / consistent / inconclusive / contradicted / open. value, se and expected are in 'unit'; z = |value - expected| / se. python -m mppp_studies.validation.ledger writes the table of the final report.

entries.claim: The Mastcam-Z 34 mm rig pitch rises with sol (joint, Navcam held: +5.4 +- 1.5 mdeg / 1000 sols)
entries.test: test 3: ZL-ZR pairs alone (no Navcam, no bundle adjustment); 33 pairs, 13 blocks, sols 11-1882
entries.note: A drift exists without the Navcam (3.7 sigma from zero). Linear rate 1.3 sigma above the joint's; after sol 250 alone +6.3 +- 5.0. The pairs measure pitch + (dcy_R - dcy_L) / f. Pair-to-pair scatter 8 mdeg (0.7 px), 80 times the formal error: a sequence-level effect not explained by focus.

entries.claim: The Mastcam-Z 110 mm rig pitch rises with sol (joint: +5.3 +- 1.7 mdeg / 1000 sols)
entries.test: test 3: ZL-ZR pairs alone; 11 pairs, 6 blocks, sols 78-1964
entries.note: 4.6 sigma from zero; 2.4 sigma above the joint's linear rate. With the sol-250 knee: +8.2 +- 3.1 after it, +40 +- 21 more before it - the Navcam law's shape (+22.6 before, +5.6 after). Only 11 pairs: more are needed before the size is quoted.

entries.claim: The drift is a rotation of the cameras, not a principal-point (detector) shift inside each camera
entries.test: test 3 across zooms: one camera, one detector, two focal lengths - a rotation gives one rate in mdeg, a detector shift one rate in px
entries.note: In pixels the rates differ by 3.4 sigma (0.68 +- 0.18 against 2.94 +- 0.64); in mdeg by 0.9 sigma (8.2 +- 2.2 against 11.4 +- 2.5). A shift that scales with the zoom's focal length is not excluded by this.

entries.claim: The Mastcam-Z rig drift is not a leak from the Navcam rig law held in the joints
entries.test: test 3 uses no Navcam frame and no Navcam model
entries.note: A leak would give no drift in pairs alone. Whether the joint's SIZE carries some leak (5.4 against 8.2 +- 2.2) is open.

entries.claim: The drift is not a mis-modelled focus term
entries.test: test 3 with a focus term: w_x = a + r sol + c focus
entries.unit: mdeg / 1000 sols (34 mm, focus term in)
entries.note: 34 mm: focus term -3.6 +- 12.8 mdeg / 1000 counts, the rate unchanged. 110 mm: a real focus term, -10.0 +- 2.6 mdeg / 1000 counts (2.6 px: the eyes' vertical alignment moves with focus), the rate +10.9 +- 1.6 with it.

entries.claim: The Navcam focal length rises by 34.5 ppm / degC (the law's thermal term)
entries.test: test 4: single Navcam frames resected on >= 5 surveyed deck targets, pose and one focal scale free; 92 frames, 77 sols, -28.5 to -5 degC
entries.unit: ppm / degC left over with the law applied
entries.note: Zero within 1.7 sigma; a constant focal length (-34.5) is 2.9 sigma away. NR alone -3 +- 23, NL +60 +- 40, frames with >= 6 targets +4 +- 28 (1.4 sigma from -34.5). Independent of the baseline and of the deck's own expansion. Needs under 10 ppm / degC: more frames with five targets, colder ones (none below -28.5 degC qualifies).

entries.claim: The Navcam focal length at -20 degC
entries.test: test 4, the level of the focal scale
entries.unit: ppm above the law, at 0.8-2.4 m
entries.note: Not a claim against the law: at 1-2 m a fisheye's entrance pupil moves with field angle and the level depends on the survey's shape (AFT1). Listed so it is not forgotten.

entries.claim: The head pitch drift after the knee is +5.6 mdeg / 1000 sols
entries.test: Navcam ties (+5.57 +- 0.20), deck fiducials DJ32 (+6.6), Mastcam-Z joints 34 / 110 mm (+5.4 +- 1.5, +5.3 +- 1.7)
entries.note: The deck value's se was not carried into the note.

entries.test: the azimuth resolver over full turns (DJ32 chain): k_az
entries.note: The se must be taken from the DJ32 solution before this is quoted.

entries.claim: The Navcam baseline is 423.53 mm at -20 degC
entries.note: Shares the survey's thermal state with the six targets.

entries.claim: A 34 mm 360 taken after a 48 mm calibration-target observation is in the high backlash state (the zoom history alone decides; neither a calibration target nor a drive parks the zoom at 26 mm)
entries.test: the 12 Nov 34 mm joint's sequence offsets of the rule-test sequences labelled high
entries.unit: ppm from the high line (ZCAM08692, 107 frames)
entries.note: ZCAM08692 -110 / -98 ppm, ZCAM08808 +1006 / +703, ZCAM09938 +1571 / +1504 (the low line is about -8700). Drive rule: ZCAM07111 -1864 / -1936 (a fifth of the gap). Open: ZCAM08401 -4453 / -3938, half the gap.
